coverage_rule: Include every named individual dramatic character directly named in the accessible official English profile or episode metadata for the specified opening segment. Only Mori Jin is named there. Tournament structure, judges, organizations, borrowed power, techniques, objects, places, roles, peoples/species, and unnamed participants remain terms or omissions.
omissions: All other opening-segment characters and every later character are omitted because the accessible English profile/episode metadata does not name them claim by claim and visual/webtoon panels were not transcribed.
Borrowed power, organization names, techniques, artifacts, plot turns, wider mythology, and later godhood material are not asserted from this opening evidence.
Korean original-platform wording, alternate romanizations/Korean script, anime, games, soundtrack, merchandise, and adaptations are separate witnesses.

The high-school tournament/action premise supports an age-sensitive youth-and-fighting caution, but no particular injuries, death, sexual content, or detailed violence is inferred from uninspected episodes.
uncertainties: WEBTOON supplies an exact viewer route for each episode but browser-readable captures expose episode number/creator rather than dialogue or panels; this is a narrow official-metadata pass.
Mori Jin is the English profile spelling. Korean-script spelling and additional English/Korean variants require a separately inspected original Korean witness.
The global English profile says the early competition later reveals a much larger plot; that later teaser is not used as a character or system claim for Episodes 1-10.
Translated WEBTOON editions have distinct title numbers and wording; they are not treated as interchangeable with this English witness.
evidence_basis: Official WEBTOON English series/profile and episode-number metadata only; no fan wiki, Wikipedia, anime/game source, uninspected panels, or external synopsis is used.
